title: The Velveteen Rabbit
summary: A small toy rabbit hopes to become real when a young child loves him.
coverScene: A worn soft rabbit toy sits on a cozy nursery floor next to a wooden bed.

sentences.text: One day, a young child gets many things.
Most things are big and new.
One thing is a small rabbit.
The rabbit has many color parts.
Many people look away from him.
An old horse talks to him.
The horse says love makes things real.
Real things lose eye parts.
One night, the child takes the rabbit.
The rabbit stays near the child.
The child holds him very much every night.
Months pass.
The child loves the rabbit a lot.
They play in a place.
The rabbit feels very well now.
Then, a bad problem comes.
The child is very bad in bed.
The rabbit stays by his hand.
The child gets better later.
People say things must end.
They put the rabbit in a bag.
He stays outside near a place.
A real power appears then.
She makes the rabbit real.
He runs on the land.
Later, the rabbit looks at the child.
He has strong small parts now.
The child sees him outside.
The rabbit looks pleased because he is real.

sentences.text: Once, a little boy received many things during Christmas.

The animal had some dark color and nice hair on the face.
Most people did not care about the little animal in the room.
Only the old animal understood real things.
He lived in the room for years.
He explained that love made something real.
It happened when a child loved something very much.
At first, the small animal wondered about this wonder.
Then, one night, the boy took the animal to bed.
From that evening, the animal slept near the boy.
The boy held him close every single night.
Months passed, and the animal felt very happy.
The boy talked to him and took him outside.
They played long games in the garden.
The animal knew he was becoming real.
Then, a bad disease came upon the young boy.
The boy was very bad in bed.
The animal stayed near his hand through every hour.
The boy finally got better from the disease.
The doctor said they must remove all things.
They put the animal into a clothes container outside.
The poor animal dropped one water line from the eye.
A special person appeared from the plants.
She told him that she would make him real.
He changed into a living animal.
Later, the animal came back to the garden.
He looked at the boy with strong dark feet.
The boy saw him and thought he looked like someone else.
The animal smiled because he was real.
The boy and the animal were very happy.

He took the brown toy to bed instead.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a little boy received many toys during Christmas.
Most toys were modern and expensive, but one was just an animal made from soft brown skin and hair.
The animal had brown spots and short face hair, which made him look quite charming.
Among all the expensive items in the room, the animal was ignored by most people.
Only the wise old skin horse understood how toys truly became real.
The skin horse had lived in the room for years, and his brown coat was quite worn out.
He explained that becoming real was not about having metal parts or working buttons.
It happened when a child loved a toy so deeply that all its hair fell off and its eyes grew old.
At first, the animal wondered if this special change would ever happen to him.
Then, one night when the boy could not find his usual toy sheep, he took the animal to bed instead.
From that evening forward, the animal slept closely beside the boy every single night.
He was held so tightly that his nice brown coat grew thin in several spots.
As the months passed by, the animal felt more than happy because the boy loved him so much.
The boy would talk to him about everyday things and take him outside into the garden for long games.
Even though he was losing his shape, the animal did not care about that physical change.
He knew that he was becoming real, exactly as the skin horse had promised him long ago.
Then, a terrible illness came upon the young boy, making him very weak and sick in bed.
The animal stayed beside his small hand throughout every difficult hour of the high temperature.
When the boy finally got better, the doctor said that the room and all its toys must be burned.
Because the illness could spread, everything used by the sick child had to be destroyed safely.
They put the animal into a bag with old clothes, leaving him behind near the garden outside.
As the poor little animal shed a tear, a bright spirit appeared from the flowers.
She told him that because he had been truly loved, she would take him away and make him real.
He was changed into a living animal who could run freely through the green grass.
After some time had passed, the animal came back to the garden to look at the boy.
He looked just like the old toy that the child had loved, but now he had strong brown legs.
When the boy saw him, he thought that the creature looked familiar, but he did not know the truth.
The animal smiled softly, knowing he was finally real.
He thought about the old room where the skin horse had told him about real life.
The boy grew older each year, but he always remembered the little toy that he had loved so deeply.
Every morning, the sun shone brightly across the green grass where the animal loved to run.
The other creatures in the forest often watched him as he moved so quickly through the trees.
They did not know that he had once been a soft toy sitting quietly upon a child's bed.
The animal often looked back toward the house where the boy lived with his family.
He knew that their special friendship would never truly end, even though they were now apart.
Sometimes the boy would walk into the garden and look around the lovely green trees.
He would feel a strange feeling in his heart, though he could not explain the feeling.
The animal would stay very still behind a large plant while the boy stood near him.
If the boy had known the truth, he would have smiled with great joy.
Instead, he just breathed the fresh air and walked slowly back inside his house.
The animal watched him go and then returned to his daily play among the flowers.
Life in the garden was full of wonderful sights and sounds for a creature that could finally run.
He felt the cool wind against his face and thanked the bright spirit for her wonderful gift.
No one could ever take away the love that the boy had given him during those quiet nights.
That love was the magic which had transformed his soft body into a strong, living animal.
Years passed by like a gentle river, bringing peace and happiness to both the boy and his old friend.
And so the story of the little toy lived on in the hearts of those who truly believed in love.
He ran through the green grass every day, feeling free and happy under the bright sun.
The other animals watched him from afar, wondering who he was and where he came from.
He never forgot the boy who had loved him so much when they were together in the house.
Every single moment was filled with joy because he was finally a real and living creature.
The bright spirit had given him a wonderful new life, and he thanked her every single day.
His heart was full of peace as he ran across the green field under the blue sky.

options: Because the boy had a terrible illness
Because the boy did not like them

sentences.text: Amidst the glittering chaos of Christmas morning, a little boy received an abundance of modern and expensive toys.
Most of them were marvels of tin and wind-up mechanisms, designed to impress with flashing lights and mechanical precision.
Yet tucked quietly among the glittering novelties was an unassuming creature fashioned entirely from soft brown velvet.
He possessed endearing brown spots and a short dusting of facial hair that gave him a remarkably charming expression.
Despite the intricate marvels occupying the nursery floor, this quiet plush animal was almost entirely overlooked by the adults.
Only the wise old skin horse, whose faded coat bore witness to years of faithful service, understood the mysterious nature of toys.
He had occupied a prominent corner of the room for so long that his brown felt was worn bare in patches, revealing his seams.
When the newcomer asked about the secrets of the nursery, the old horse explained that becoming real was no simple matter of gears.
It had nothing to do with mechanical joints, painted buttons, or how much a contraption cost at the holiday bazaar.
Realness was something that only happened after a child loved an object so deeply that its exterior grew worn and thin.
At first, the little velvet animal wondered if such a wondrous transformation would ever occur within his own quiet existence.
Then, on a restless evening when the boy could not locate his usual woolly sheep, he reached out for the rabbit instead.
From that memorable night onward, the plush creature became an inseparable companion, sharing the warmth of the small bed.
He was held so tightly through the dark hours that his once-sleek brown coat began to thin across his chest and paws.
As the quiet months drifted past, the rabbit felt a profound sense of contentment simply because the boy cherished him so completely.
The child would murmur quiet secrets into the velvet ear and carry his companion out into the garden for long, imaginative games.
Even though the rabbit gradually lost his pristine shape and his stuffing shifted awkwardly, he cared nothing for these physical changes.
He knew with absolute certainty that he was becoming real, exactly as the skin horse had prophesied during their midnight conversations.
Then, without warning, a severe illness descended upon the young household, rendering the little boy burning hot and desperately weak.
Through every grueling hour of the fever, the faithful rabbit remained clutched tightly against the small, restless hand.
When the crisis finally broke and the child began the slow journey toward recovery, the strict family doctor issued a harsh decree.
Because the microscopic germs of the contagion lingered, the nursery and all its contents presented a severe danger to the household.
Everything that had touched the sick child during his ordeal had to be gathered up and safely destroyed by fire.
The rabbit was unceremoniously tossed into a large sack alongside discarded winter clothes and carried out near the garden gate.
As he lay abandoned in the damp grass, a single tear traced a damp path down his velvet cheek.
In that moment of profound sorrow, a shimmering light flickered among the flowerbeds and coalesced into a radiant woodland spirit.
She looked down at the forlorn little toy with immense kindness, acknowledging that he had served the ultimate purpose of love.
Because he had been held so dear by a human child, she declared that she would now elevate him to a higher existence.
With a gentle sweep of her hand, she transformed his stiff plush body into a living creature with powerful muscles and keen senses.
He leaped away from the garden path, discovering for the first time the exhilarating freedom of running across the dew-kissed grass.
After some time had passed and his new life had settled into a rhythm, the rabbit ventured back toward the familiar garden.
Peering through the wooden fence, he caught sight of a growing boy who bore a striking resemblance to his former master.
Though his new form was strong and wild, his face still retained the gentle contours of the beloved toy left behind.
When the young boy glanced in his direction, a flicker of recognition crossed his features, though he could not fathom the truth.
The rabbit smiled softly to himself, resting comfortably in the knowledge that the old nursery magic had finally been fulfilled.
The boy grew taller with each passing season, yet he never quite forgot the worn velvet companion of his early childhood.
Whenever he wandered through the garden paths, he would occasionally pause, feeling a strange and unaccountable warmth in his chest.
He could not explain the sudden yearning that seized him, nor could he guess that the agile creature watching him from the bushes was his toy.
If the child had only known the miraculous truth, he would have dropped to his knees with overwhelming joy and disbelief.
Instead, he merely breathed in the fragrant air of the afternoon and strolled slowly back toward the warmth of the house.
The rabbit watched the familiar figure depart, then turned to rejoin the lively community of creatures inhabiting the sunny meadows.
Every waking hour was filled with breathtaking sights, the rush of cool wind, and the intoxicating scent of wildflowers.
He frequently glanced back toward the distant house, deeply grateful for the profound bond that had bridged two entirely different worlds.
No amount of time could ever erase the memory of those quiet nights spent in the narrow bed holding a sleeping child.
That selfless devotion had been the catalyst, the hidden spark that turned fabric and stuffing into a beating heart.
Generations of wild creatures watched him dash effortlessly between the ancient trees, never guessing his humble origins.
He thrived under the open sky, bounding across green pastures with an exuberance that made the entire world seem fresh.
Whenever the sun rose over the rolling hills, it illuminated a landscape of peace and enduring harmony for the transformed rabbit.
He whispered a daily word of thanks to the radiant spirit who had granted him such an extraordinary second chance at life.
His spirit remained anchored both to the vibrant present and to the cherished memories of the nursery room long ago.

quiz.q: What initial explanation did the skin horse give regarding how a toy becomes real?
options: It happens when a child loves a toy so much that its exterior wears out.

quiz.q: Why was the rabbit ultimately removed from the nursery and placed near the garden gate?
options: The family was moving to a different house and forgot to pack him.
The doctor ordered that everything the sick child touched must be destroyed.
The boy grew too old for toys and decided to donate his old belongings.

quiz.q: What happened to the rabbit immediately after he shed a tear by the garden gate?
options: He was rescued by the family doctor and placed back inside the nursery.
A radiant woodland spirit appeared and transformed him into a living animal.
The young boy found him in the sack and carried him back to his bed.
